questions.question: You’re running late for an important meeting. Your colleague says, *'I’m sorry I’m late—my train was delayed by half an hour.'* How would you best respond if you wanted to take some of the blame while offering a polite solution?
options: That’s okay, but we should still leave early tomorrow to make up for lost time.
It’s not your fault—trains are always late! Let’s just focus on the meeting.
I’m really sorry about that—maybe we should discuss this in the morning?
Don’t worry, I’ll make sure we’re on time next time.
questions.answer: I’m really sorry about that—maybe we should discuss this in the morning?

questions.question: A friend asks you, *'Do you think it’s a good idea to move to London for work?'* What would be the most appropriate way to express your opinion while suggesting alternatives?
options: I don’t know—I’ve never lived there, but maybe you should ask your boss first.
I’m not sure, but London is expensive, so perhaps you should consider a smaller city instead.
Yes, it’s a great opportunity, but you should definitely get a mortgage first.
No, it’s not a good idea—you’ll regret it in the end.
questions.answer: I’m not sure, but London is expensive, so perhaps you should consider a smaller city instead.

questions.question: Your boss asks you to help organise the team’s annual picnic. What would be the most appropriate way to respond if you’re unsure whether you can commit?
options: Sure, I’ll help—it sounds like fun!
I’d love to, but I’m not sure if I can make it all weekend.
That’s a great idea, but I’ve already got plans for the weekend.
I’m not sure if I can do that—I have other commitments.
questions.answer: I’d love to, but I’m not sure if I can make it all weekend.

questions.question: A customer at a café asks, *'Could you remind me how much this coffee costs?'* What would be the most polite way to respond, given the café is closed for the day?
options: I’m sorry, we’re closed today—you can order online if you like.
It’s £3, but we don’t take cards here.
We don’t serve coffee today—try the bakery next door instead.
You can pay £3 now, and I’ll make it for you.
questions.answer: I’m sorry, we’re closed today—you can order online if you like.

questions.question: You’re at a formal dinner and your neighbour says, *'I’ve heard a lot about your new project—it sounds fascinating!'* How would you best respond to express enthusiasm while politely agreeing with their opinion?
options: Oh, it’s not really that interesting—I’m just working on a small task.
Yes, it’s very interesting, but I’m not sure how it will work out.
Thank you, it’s been a long time coming, and I’m really excited to share it with you.
I’m not sure if it’s really fascinating—maybe you should ask someone else.
questions.answer: Thank you, it’s been a long time coming, and I’m really excited to share it with you.
